Then and now

Notch's entry for the Java 4K contest, released in December 2009, drew a small world with a CPU raycaster. This one hands both the world and the rays to the GPU.

2009 Java 4KThis
Size2581 B Java applet4085 B HTML
World64 x 64 x 631024 x 1024 x 128 (128 MiB)
RendererCPU raycaster at about 214 x 120WebGPU compute shader at full window resolution
GenerationCPU at loadcompute shader at load
Placeablegrass16: 3 plants, 10 blocks, 3 ores
Lightingface shadingambient occlusion, sun shadows, day and night

How it fits

The page is a decoder and a deflate stream. The decoder is all the page can afford, so everything else is squeezed before it gets there.

  1. Source

    TypeScript for the game and WGSL for the shader. World constants are shared by name.

  2. Shrink

    An in-house minifier rewrites the AST and picks every name by deflate size, the shader's names too.

  3. Deflate

    An in-house encoder searches the bit stream for one without the 10 bytes the parser or l9 would change, against zopfli and libdeflate.

  4. Page

    charset=l9 reads each byte as one character. The stream sits raw in <canvas><xmp>.

  5. Boot

    The browser inflates it with DecompressionStream('deflate-raw') and evals the result.

<meta charset=l9><body onload='new Response(new Response(Uint8Array.from(c.textContent,c=>c.charCodeAt())).body.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("deflate-raw"))).text().then(eval)'><canvas id=c><xmp>

Then the raw deflate stream. No decompressor, no zlib header.

The whole packer, with byte maps and charts: A Deflate Stream Without 10 Bytes on ayfri.com.

Requirements

Needs WebGPU with immediates, a keyboard and a mouse. Today that means Chrome 150+ on Windows or macOS.

BrowserRunsWhy
Chrome 150+ on Windowsyestested on Chrome 155
Chrome 150+ on macOSyestested by a player
Edge 150+, Chrome on Linux, ChromeOSshoulduntested, same engine
Firefox 158nono immediates, tested: everything else works
Safari 26nono immediates
Phones, tabletsnothe controls need a keyboard and a mouse

Immediates are the tiny per-dispatch uniforms set with setImmediates and read as var<immediate> in WGSL. They save the bytes of a uniform buffer.
